title: A Conformal Martingales Approach for Recurrent Concept Drift
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 266, Conformal and Probabilistic Prediction with Applications
tldr: Pool ICM framework reuses previously trained models upon recurrent concept drift detection, cutting retraining events by up to 94% with less than 3 percentage points accuracy loss.
problem_and_motivation: In data stream classification, recurrent concept drift causes previously seen distributions to reappear. Existing methods retrain after every detected drift, wasting computational resources even when a previously trained model could be reused.
approach: Extends Inductive Conformal Martingales (ICM) for concept drift detection with model reuse capability.
Upon drift detection, selects model from a pool if ICM fails to reject exchangeability between recent data and the model's training window.
Second criterion: model's F1 score on current window exceeds a threshold from historical performance.
Trains new model only when no stored model satisfies both criteria.
Evaluated on STAGGER, Airlines, and ELEC public data streams.
findings: num: Cuts retraining events by up to 94% compared to always retraining.
num: Reduces wasted training instances by 22-33%.
num: Limits accuracy loss to less than 3 percentage points relative to always retraining.

definitions.definition: Type of concept drift where previously seen data distributions reappear over time.
Extended Inductive Conformal Martingales framework enabling model reuse upon recurrent drift.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Introduces a novel approach to handling recurrent concept drift that reuses previously trained models. The dual-criteria selection combining exchangeability testing with performance evaluation is original. Demonstrates significant computational savings with minimal accuracy trade-off.
directly_justifies: Model reuse upon recurrent drift cuts retraining events by up to 94%.
Exchangeability testing effectively identifies previously seen concepts for model reuse.
limits: Not evaluated in personal finance or spending data contexts.
Accuracy slightly below approaches that always retrain.

limitations: Accuracy slightly below approaches that always retrain on every drift.
Evaluated on only three benchmark datasets.
